body:
## Problem

The package ships `"postinstall": "node scripts/postinstall.cjs"`. pnpm 12 fails the install with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` for any dependency with an unapproved build script; Yarn 4 defaults to `enableScripts: false` and skips it. `README.md:27` promises "After installing it, a _`.prettierrc.json`_ file will be created automatically".

## Evidence

Consumer installs of `@ivuorinen/prettier-config` in empty scratch projects (pnpm 12.4.1, Yarn 4.18.0, npm 11.19.0):

```text
$ pnpm add -D @ivuorinen/prettier-config
Error: ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS
  ╰─▶ Ignored build scripts: @ivuorinen/prettier-config 2.0.12   → exit 1
$ CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile        → exit 1, ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS
$ pnpm add -D prettier                          # control → exit 0
$ yarn add -D @ivuorinen/prettier-config        # Yarn 4
YN0004: … lists build scripts, but all build scripts have been disabled.  → exit 0, .prettierrc.json: NO
$ npm install --save-dev @ivuorinen/prettier-config
exit 0, .prettierrc.json: YES, warns install-scripts not yet covered by allowScripts
```

## Impact

pnpm 12 consumers cannot install the package at all without `pnpm approve-builds`; Yarn 4 consumers get no `.prettierrc.json`, so Prettier formats with its defaults (double quotes, semicolons, trailing commas) — the opposite of this config — without any error.

## Fix

Replace the `postinstall` with an explicit initializer `bin` (e.g. `npx prettier-config-init`) and document writing `.prettierrc.json` containing `"@ivuorinen/prettier-config"` by hand. If the postinstall stays, document the pnpm and Yarn 4 behaviour in the README.

## Resolution
Owner chose the document-only fix: README tells users to create .prettierrc.json and states npm runs the postinstall (with an allowScripts warning), Yarn 4 does not, and pnpm fails until `pnpm approve-builds` (verified on pnpm 12.4.1). Postinstall unchanged by owner decision.
title: postinstall breaks pnpm 12 installs and never runs under Yarn 4, contrary to the README

## Problem

Dependency vulnerability. `yarn.lock` resolves `pacote` 21.4.0 (via `@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config` → `semantic-release` → `npm`), affected by GHSA-w4pp-8pjf-rmxw / CVE-2026-9496 (High, fixed in 21.5.1).

## Evidence

osv-scanner 2.6.0 (`GHSA-w4pp-8pjf-rmxw`, HIGH) and `yarn npm audit --all --recursive` (advisory 1146559, `vulnerable: >=11.2.7 <21.5.1`, tree 21.4.0).

## Impact

Vulnerable tarball handling executes in the release job.

## Fix

`yarn up -R pacote` (or `resolutions: { "pacote": "^21.5.1" }`), `yarn install`, re-scan.

## Resolution
yarn up -R pacote tar: pacote now 21.5.1. osv-scanner: No issues found.
title: pacote 21.4.0 is vulnerable to GHSA-w4pp-8pjf-rmxw (High)

body:
## Problem

Ad-hoc unpinned package. `publish.yml:59-61` runs `npm install -g corepack --force && corepack enable` — the latest corepack with lifecycle scripts enabled — inside the job holding `NPM_TOKEN`, `secrets.PAT` and `id-token: write`. `.github/zizmor.yml` suppresses `adhoc-packages` for `publish.yml`.

## Evidence

```yaml
# .github/workflows/publish.yml:59-61
      - name: Install and enable corepack
        shell: sh
        run: npm install -g corepack --force && corepack enable
```

`base-configs-stylelint` pins this step and adds `--ignore-scripts`.

## Impact

A malicious or broken corepack release executes with release credentials in scope and decides which Yarn builds the release.

## Fix

On this repo's Node 24 (`.nvmrc` `v24`, which bundles corepack) replace the step with `corepack enable`; otherwise pin it with `--ignore-scripts`.

## Resolution
publish.yml now runs `corepack enable` (Node 24 from .nvmrc bundles it); publish.yml dropped from the zizmor adhoc-packages ignore. actionlint and zizmor --pedantic clean.
title: Release job npm-installs a floating corepack with install scripts enabled

body:
## Problem

`publish.yml:63-73` restores `node_modules` keyed on `hashFiles('**/yarn.lock')` and runs `yarn install` only on a cache miss, without `--immutable`. A `package.json`-only change or `.nvmrc` bump keeps the key and releases from a stale tree.

## Evidence

```yaml
          key: node-modules-${{ hashFiles('**/yarn.lock') }}
      - name: Install Dependencies
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: yarn install
```

`base-configs-stylelint/.github/workflows/publish.yml:86-93` records this pattern shipping a wrong release (1.4.0).

## Impact

semantic-release can apply stale release rules from `node_modules` and publish the wrong version.

## Fix

Run `yarn install --immutable --mode=skip-build` unconditionally and add `.nvmrc` to the cache key.

## Resolution
publish.yml install runs unconditionally as `yarn install --immutable --mode=skip-build`; cache key includes .nvmrc.
title: Release install is skipped on a cache hit keyed only on yarn.lock and is not --immutable

body:
## Problem

`.github/renovate.json` lacks the `packageRules` entry that gives GitHub Actions and pre-commit updates the `actions` scope; a major action bump becomes `chore(deps)!: …`, which the shared release rules map to `major`.

## Evidence

This repo's `v1.0.0` came from commits including `aa3f550 chore(deps)!: update actions/checkout (v5.0.0 → v6.0.0) (#73)`, `d61f0df chore(deps)!: update github/codeql-action (v3.30.7 → v4.30.7) (#49)` and `f4d0655 chore(deps)!: update pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks (v5.0.0 → v6.0.0) (#23)`.

## Impact

The next major action or hook bump publishes a new major of `@ivuorinen/prettier-config` with no consumer-visible change.

## Fix

Add `"packageRules": [{ "matchManagers": ["github-actions", "pre-commit"], "semanticCommitType": "chore", "semanticCommitScope": "actions" }]`.

## Resolution
Added the packageRules entry giving github-actions and pre-commit updates semanticCommitType chore, scope actions.
title: Renovate CI-only major bumps are labelled chore(deps)! and would cut a major release

body:
## Problem

Incorrect example. `README.md:33-44` tells users who need overrides to write a `.prettierrc.js` using `module.exports = { ...require("@ivuorinen/prettier-config"), … }`. In any project with `"type": "module"` a `.js` file is ESM, so `module` and `require` are undefined.

## Evidence

Consumer reproduction (npm 11.19, Prettier 3, `package.json` with `"type": "module"`, the README snippet saved as `.prettierrc.js`):

```text
$ npx prettier a.js
[error] Invalid configuration for file ".../a.js":
[error] module is not defined in ES module scope
exit 2
```

## Impact

Users following the only documented customization path in an ESM project (increasingly the default) get a Prettier crash.

## Fix

Use a format-independent file name and ESM syntax in the example:

```js
// prettier.config.mjs
import ivuorinen from '@ivuorinen/prettier-config'

export default {
  ...ivuorinen,
  semi: true,
}
```

(or keep the CommonJS version but name it `.prettierrc.cjs`).

## Resolution
README override example rewritten as prettier.config.mjs with ESM import/export. Verified in scratch consumers with "type": "module" and "type": "commonjs": `npx prettier a.js` prints `const a = 'x';` in both (shared singleQuote plus the semi override).
title: README's .prettierrc.js override example fails in ESM projects

body:
## Problem

Broken links. `README.md:68` defines `[license-link]: ./LICENSE`, but the file is `LICENSE.md`; `README.md:65` defines `[contributing-link]: https://github.com/ivuorinen/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md`, which does not exist.

## Evidence

```text
$ git ls-files | grep -i license
LICENSE.md
$ gh api repos/ivuorinen/.github/contents/CONTRIBUTING.md
Not Found (HTTP 404)
```

The sibling READMEs (commitlint, eslint, markdownlint, semantic-release) already use `./LICENSE.md`.

## Impact

The MIT badge and the License section link to a 404 on GitHub and npm, as does the contributing link.

## Fix

Change `[license-link]` to `./LICENSE.md`; add `CONTRIBUTING.md` to `ivuorinen/.github` or drop the contribution-guidelines clause.

## Resolution
[license-link] now ./LICENSE.md; contribution-guidelines clause and the dead ivuorinen/.github CONTRIBUTING.md link removed.
title: README license and contributing links point to files that do not exist

body:
## Problem

Coverage gap on a non-critical path. The suite (`test/postinstall.test.mjs`) exercises only the install script. Nothing loads `@ivuorinen/prettier-config` through its own name, so the `exports` map (`import` → `wrapper.mjs`, `require` → `index.cjs`) and the `files` allowlist are never verified.

## Evidence

Mutation check: pointing an `exports` condition at a missing file, or dropping an entry file from `files`, leaves `yarn test` at `pass 4, fail 0`. The sibling `base-configs-stylelint` shipped exactly this defect class (`exports["./css"]` pointed at the SCSS files through 1.3.5, fixed in 71799ce), and `base-configs-commitlint/test/resolve.test.mjs` resolves its package by name for that reason.

## Impact

A broken entry point reaches npm with a green suite; every consumer install then fails to load the config.

## Fix

Add `test/resolve.test.mjs` that resolves `@ivuorinen/prettier-config` by name via `createRequire(import.meta.url)` (CJS) and `await import()` (ESM) and asserts each returns the expected value, plus `npm pack --dry-run --json` asserting every file referenced by `exports` is in the tarball.

## Resolution
Added test/resolve.test.mjs resolving @ivuorinen/prettier-config by name via require and import. Passes (2/2); breaking exports.import fails 1 test, breaking exports.require fails 2 (restored after).
title: No test resolves the published entry points, so an exports-map break would ship green

body:
## Problem

Non-gating check. `pr-lint.yml`, `codeql.yml` and the new `test.yml` run on `pull_request`, but `main` is unprotected and has no rulesets, while `allow_auto_merge` is `true`.

## Evidence

```text
$ gh api repos/ivuorinen/base-configs-prettier/branches/main/protection → Branch not protected
$ gh api repos/ivuorinen/base-configs-prettier/rules/branches/main      → []
$ gh api repos/ivuorinen/base-configs-prettier --jq .allow_auto_merge   → true
```

## Impact

Failing lint, CodeQL or tests do not stop a merge; auto-merged bot PRs publish on the next push.

## Fix

Add a ruleset on `main` requiring `PR Lint`, `Analyze (javascript)` and the `Test (Node …)` checks once `test.yml` lands; verify with `gh api repos/ivuorinen/base-configs-prettier/rules/branches/main`.

## Resolution
ruleset 'main checks' (24025413) added on 2026-09-26: PR Lint, Analyze (javascript), Test (Node 20/22/24/26); verified via rules/branches/main
title: No check is required on main and auto-merge is on, so red PRs merge (verified)

body:
## Problem

The non-releasing rule in `.github/renovate.json` matches only `"matchManagers": ["github-actions", "pre-commit"]`, and the major-prefix rule only `["pre-commit"]`. Renovate's `nvm` manager, which updates `.nvmrc`, matches neither. `.nvmrc` is not in `package.json` `files`, and the workflows read it only through `node-version-file`, so a Node bump there never reaches consumers. Renovate still titles it with the preset default scope `deps`.

## Evidence

- Shared preset `github>ivuorinen/renovate-config` sets `semanticCommitScope: "actions"` only for `matchManagers: ["github-actions"]`, and sets `commitMessagePrefix: "chore(deps)!: "` on every `major` update. Its `chore(actions): ` override for majors covers github-actions only.
- Shared release rules (`@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config` 3.0.0 `index.cjs:11-13`): `chore(deps)` gives a patch, breaking `chore(deps)` gives a major, and `chore(actions)` gives no release.
- Observed: ivuorinen/base-configs#577 and ivuorinen/base-configs-commitlint#196 (branch `renovate/node-26.x`, which changes only `.nvmrc`). Renovate titled both `chore(deps): update node.js (…)`, including force-pushes made after the actions/devDependencies rule landed (#578 / #201). The maintainer renamed both to `chore(actions): …` by hand before merging (PR timeline `renamed` events by the maintainer).

## Impact

Unless someone retitles the PR, every Node minor or patch bump merges as `chore(deps)` and publishes a needless patch release. In config-checker, each release then fans out into Renovate bumps across every @ivuorinen package. A Node major (for example 26 → 28) arrives as `chore(deps)!:` and publishes a **major** release of the package, even though consumers see no change.

## Fix

Add `"nvm"` to both manager lists, and update the first rule's description so it names `.nvmrc` as well:

```json
"matchManagers": ["github-actions", "nvm", "pre-commit"],
…
"matchManagers": ["nvm", "pre-commit"],
"matchUpdateTypes": ["major"],
"commitMessagePrefix": "chore(actions): "
```

The better fix is to make the same change once in the shared `ivuorinen/renovate-config` preset, next to its github-actions major rule, so all nine repos pick it up.

## Resolution
Fixed in the shared preset, ivuorinen/renovate-config#114 (merged as 503bbff): nvm (.nvmrc) and pre-commit updates get the literal prefix "chore(tooling): " and devDependencies/require-dev get "chore(dev-deps): " for every update type, so none carries the global "chore(deps)!: " major marker; "actions" stays reserved for github-actions. @ivuorinen/semantic-release-config releases on the deps scope only, so tooling and dev-deps commits cut no release (checked through commit-analyzer). ivuorinen/base-configs-prettier#230 then removed every local scope, prefix and group rule from this repo's .github/renovate.json, which now only extends the shared preset.
title: Renovate .nvmrc (nvm manager) updates are titled chore(deps) and release the package

body:
## Problem

Excess secret exposure. `publish.yml:15-16` puts `NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}` in the workflow-level `env:`, so the `Linter` job — which runs `ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint` (MegaLinter and its bundled tools) — receives the publish credential. Only the Semantic Release step needs it, and with `id-token: write` already granted it could use OIDC trusted publishing instead (`setup-node` runs `always-auth: true`; `.github/zizmor.yml` suppresses `use-trusted-publishing` as "tracked separately").

## Evidence

semgrep and opengrep (`gha-workflow-env-secret`, WARNING) at `publish.yml:16`; manual sweep confirms the `Linter` job (lines 19-31) inherits it. `base-configs-stylelint/.github/workflows/publish.yml:15-17` documents the fix.

## Impact

A compromised lint action or MegaLinter tool can exfiltrate a token that publishes `@ivuorinen/prettier-config` on every push to `main`.

## Fix

Remove the workflow-level `env:` block and set `NPM_TOKEN` only on the Semantic Release step — or complete trusted publishing, drop `always-auth` and `NPM_TOKEN`, and delete the secret.

## Resolution
Removed the workflow-level env block from publish.yml; NPM_TOKEN now appears only on the Semantic Release step, so the Linter job no longer receives it. OIDC trusted publishing and secret deletion remain the owner's action. Later, on 2026-09-26, #229 (b3a6fcd) completed both: publish.yml now publishes through OIDC trusted publishing (id-token: write), with NPM_TOKEN and always-auth removed, and the NPM_TOKEN repository secret no longer exists (checked 2026-10-01).
title: NPM_TOKEN is set workflow-wide in publish.yml and reaches the third-party lint action
